author: Linnaeus, 1758
summary: 소나무 숲을 좋아하는 새로, 해바라기 씨를 즐겨 먹고 단풍나무·자작나무·느릅나무의 싹도 먹는다. 온순하고 움직임이 적은 편이며, 목에 있는 작은 주머니에 좋은 먹이를 채워 넣기 때문에 비슷한 크기의 새보다 먹는 데 훨씬 오래 머문다. 세계적으로는 아시아 북부, 유럽 북부, 북아메리카 등지에 분포한다.

points.en: pale buff head, rump and underparts (female)

sexes.female: 수컷보다 훨씬 회색빛이 돌고, 머리와 허리, 아랫면이 엷은 황갈색을 띤다.

art.subject: Pine Grosbeak (Pinicola enucleator), adult male in winter, a vagrant in Korean conifer forest: head, breast, rump and much of the back rosy red, the mantle feathers with darker grey centres giving a mottled look; flanks and lower belly grey; wings blackish with two bold white wing bars and white edges to the tertials, so three white lines show on the folded wing; tail blackish, long and notched. Bill short, stubby and deep, blackish-grey, with a curved culmen and a small hooked tip; eye dark; legs blackish.
art.pose: perched quietly on a pine branch, nibbling buds
art.scene: Korean pine forest with dense conifer branches; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched: plump body and long notched tail, rosy-red head, breast, rump and mottled back, grey flanks and belly, blackish wings with two white wing bars and white-edged tertials forming three white lines, stubby hooked dark bill

adult female, side view perched: grey body with olive-yellow to ochre head and rump, grey underparts with a faint ochre wash on the breast, the same blackish wings with two white wing bars and white tertial edges, same stubby dark bill
art.build: A large, plump, long-tailed finch, much bigger than a sparrow and about starling-sized but bulkier and longer-tailed; round head, short thick neck, upright and slow-moving, often very tame. Bill short, stubby and deep with a strongly curved culmen ending in a small hook, shorter than the head. Legs short, blackish. Tail long for a finch and notched at the tip. In flight undulating, the white wing bars obvious.
avoid: Do not paint a huge conical bill like a Hawfinch or crossed mandibles like a crossbill; the bill is short, stubby and slightly hooked.
Do not paint the male red all over including the belly; the flanks and belly are grey.
Do not make it a small, compact finch; it is large and long-tailed, unlike the much smaller rosefinches.
Do not paint thin or missing wing bars; the two white bars and white tertial edges are bold.
